claims.text: Pre-coating tungsten particles with a nanostructured refractory HEA interphase will reduce the interfacial thermal resistance between tungsten and copper.
Reducing W–Cu interfacial thermal resistance with the HEA coating will increase the composite's thermal conductivity.
The HEA coating can increase thermal conductivity without compromising mechanical durability.
The HEA coating can increase thermal conductivity without compromising irradiation resistance.
Conventional W–Cu composites have high interfacial resistance to electron-mediated heat transfer.
A 5–20 nm nanostructured HEA layer can be deposited on tungsten particles by sputtering before consolidation.
A refractory HEA based on Cr–Fe–Ti–Ta–W is a suitable candidate interphase material.
The proposed processing will produce a coherent, uniformly deposited, defect-minimized HEA interphase at the W–Cu interface.
A coherent HEA interphase will reduce electron scattering at the W–Cu interface.
The HEA provides an improved electronic-structure match between tungsten and copper.
Improved electronic-structure matching lowers W–Cu interfacial thermal resistance by reducing electron scattering.
A particle coating can improve interfacial bonding and mechanical properties relative to an uncoated composite.
Refractory Cr–Fe–Ti–Ta–W HEAs possess sufficient high-temperature stability to help sustain interfacial integrity.
Refractory Cr–Fe–Ti–Ta–W HEAs possess irradiation-resistant properties that will preserve the W–Cu interface.
The refractory HEA interphase will hinder defect propagation.
The coated W–Cu composite will have significantly greater thermal conductivity than an otherwise comparable uncoated W–Cu composite.
Mechanical durability and irradiation resistance will be maintained or enhanced under high-temperature and irradiation exposure.
The proposed benefits should hold through approximately 1000 °C and under He+ and D+ irradiation representative of fusion-reactor environments.
Interfacial defects or nonuniform coating could negate the proposed conductivity and durability benefits.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant conductivity increase, or degradation of mechanical durability or irradiation resistance, would falsify the hypothesis.
